# User onboarding

Source: https://flows.sh/solutions/user-onboarding

## How Flows works for user onboarding

Power-up your user onboarding with flexible tools that help you create engaging experiences for your users.

### In-app product tours

Guide users step-by-step through key features for their success in your product. Highlight actions, showcase the value, and lead them to their “Aha” moment.

### Embeddable components

Embed UI elements directly into your application without needing to update code or re-deploying.

### Flexible solution

Flows comes with a set of built-in UI components to get you started. Not enough? Create your own components with custom styling and logic to create a native experience.

### Part of a workflow

Create powerful workflows that engage users at every stage of their user experience.

## Designed for unlimited customizability

Flows is designed to be a “Headless product adoption platform”. We’ll focus on user state problems, so you can focus on your own product.

## Questions and Answers

Flows is a product adoption platform that streamlines user onboarding with tools and components to guide users through key features. Integrate Flows to create in-app tours, embed UI elements, and design custom workflows to enhance engagement and retention. The visual editor allows non-developers to manage these elements without coding, while offering customization for developers.

Flows includes built-in UI components and supports custom components for a native experience. Its scalable pricing model starts with a free tier for up to 250 monthly tracked users (MTUs), making it cost-effective for businesses of all sizes.

You don’t need to know how to code to start creating user onboarding flows with Flows. Once you integrate our SDK, you can use our visual editor to create and manage workflows without writing any code.

However, Flows is a “Headless product adoption platform”, so having a front-end developer on your team can be beneficial to fully leverage its customization capabilities by creating custom UI components for your workflows

Flows are designed to be a “Headless product adoption platform“. This means that you can [create your own UI components](https://flows.sh/docs/components/custom) with custom styling and logic to create a native experience for your users. You can also use our built-in components to get started quickly.

Flows is free for up to 250 monthly tracked users (MTUs). After that, the pricing starts at $0.1 per MTU. Our pricing is volume based, so the more active users you have, the less you pay per user. For more information, check out our [pricing page](https://flows.sh/pricing).

# Product-led growth

Source: https://flows.sh/solutions/product-led-growth

## How Flows works for product-led growth

Leverage the power of Flows to build personalized growth campaigns that drive user engagement and retention.

### Personalized onboarding

Create welcome experiences and guided tutorials that turn new sign-ups into active users. Use modals, hints, or tours to highlight key features. Interactive checklists help users track their progress and stay engaged.

### In-app messages & announcements

Deliver the right message at the right moment. With Flows, you can deploy targeted banners, tooltips, and modals to announce new features or promote relevant add-ons. Automate upsell and renewal prompts based on usage data, so users get the most valuable offers.

### Fully customizable UI components

Start quickly with built-in UI elements like tooltips, hints and modals designed for engagement. Need a unique experience? Build your own components and logic to match your exact requirements. Flows APIs give you the power to build anything you need.

### Integrated growth workflows

Combine experiences into multi-step campaigns that guide users through your ideal product journey. For example, trigger a welcome modal after sign-up, then follow up with a feature tour, and later nudge with an upsell banner. Flows can branch and filter based on user attributes so you can personalize the experience.

### Embeddable components

Embed UI elements directly into your application without needing to update code or re-deploying.

## Designed for unlimited customizability

Flows is designed to be a “Headless product adoption platform”. We’ll focus on user state problems, so you can focus on your own product.

Our visual editor lets marketing and product teams build and update flows without code, while developers can add custom components for a native feel. By streamlining these experiences, Flows helps turn your product into a powerful growth engine.

You can also use our built-in components to get started quickly.

# Convert free trials to paying customers

Create strategic in-app promotions. With Flows, you can deliver the right message at the right time to drive conversion and account expansion.

Boost your MRR with contextual upgrade campaigns. Create in-app modals, banners, and other upsell prompts that convert free trial users into paying customers.

Nudge users toward higher plans when they hit value milestones. Using Flows, you can create targeted modals or banners that offer discounts or highlight premium features at the right moment. Personalize these messages by segment to make each offer more relevant.

### Feature gating & paywalls

Do you have advanced features that are only available to premium users? Use Flows to prompt lower - tier users to upgrade when they try to access these features. For example, when a free user clicks a locked feature, Flows can trigger an upgrade banner highlighting the benefits of the premium plan.

### Fully customizable UI components

Start quickly with built-in UI elements like tooltips, hints and modals designed for engagement. Need a unique look? Build your own styling and logic to match your product’s brand. Flows APIs give you the power to build anything you need.

### Integrated workflows

Integrate revenue expansion campaigns into larger user journeys. For instance, you might show an upsell banner only after a user completes onboarding, or follow a new feature announcement with a tutorial. Flows lets you sequence these touchpoints in a single workflow for maximum impact.

### Embeddable components

Embed UI elements directly into your application without needing to update code or re-deploying.

## Designed for unlimited customizability

Flows is designed to be a “Headless product adoption platform”. We’ll focus on user state problems, so you can focus on your own product.

The visual editor lets non-developers design these campaigns without code, while developers can still add custom UI components if needed. By streamlining and centralizing in-app promotions, Flows turns your product into a powerful engine for growth.

This means that you can [create your own UI components](https://flows.sh/docs/components/custom) with custom styling and logic to create a native experience for your users. You can also use our built-in components to get started quickly.

Flows is free for up to 250 monthly tracked users (MTUs). After that, the pricing starts at $0.1 per MTU. Our pricing is volume based, so the more active users you have, the less you pay per user. For more information, check out our [pricing page](https://flows.sh/pricing).

# Quickstart

Source: https://flows.sh/docs/quickstart

# Quickstart

Welcome to Flows, a fully customizable product adoption platform for modern companies building onboarding and user engagement experiences.


Flows enables you to build engaging in-app experiences—such as user onboarding and feature announcements—that help users get the most out of your product. This no-code platform empowers you to design and manage these experiences without writing code, while still offering the freedom to integrate your own custom UI components into your workflows.

Begin by installing the Flows SDK in your app. We offer SDKs tailored for both React and JavaScript applications. Follow the installation guide that matches your app’s stack, then return to this guide.


### React

The Flows SDK built specifically for React applications.


### JavaScript

The Flows SDK for integrating with any JavaScript framework.


### Next.js

React SDK integration into Next.js applications.


### Angular

JavaScript SDK integration into Angular applications.


### Vue Nuxt

JavaScript SDK integration into Nuxt applications.


### Svelte

JavaScript SDK integration into Svelte applications.


### Solid

JavaScript SDK integration into Solid applications.


### Astro

JavaScript SDK integration into Astro applications.


### Ember

JavaScript SDK integration into Ember applications.


### React Router

React SDK integration into React Router applications.


### TanStack

React SDK integration into TanStack applications.

Flows provides a set of pre-built components for your workflows, they come with good defaults, but you can customize their styles to match your brand. Check out our [styling guide](https://flows.sh/docs/blocks/basics-v2/styling) for tips on how to easily apply your own colors, fonts, and spacing to Flows components.

You’re ready to create a workflow! Navigate to **Workflows**, click **Create workflow**, and begin building. Below are some tips to help you get started, or if you'd like a step-by-step walkthrough, check out our [Create a Product Tour guide](https://flows.sh/docs/guides/create-product-tour).

Check out our [workflow examples](https://flows.sh/examples) to see what’s possible with Flows.

You’ve created your first Flows workflow. Our documentation covers everything you need to build and manage workflows, including topics like [environments](https://flows.sh/docs/environments), [creating custom components](https://flows.sh/docs/guides/create-custom-components), and [inspecting users](https://flows.sh/docs/users/overview).

If you have any questions, feel free to [contact us](https://flows.sh/contact).

# Concepts

Source: https://flows.sh/docs/concepts

# Concepts

Get a basic understanding of Flows so you can set up your organization and start using Flows effectively.


An [organization](https://flows.sh/docs/organization-setup/organizations) is the container for all workflows, environments, users, and members. As a user, you can belong to multiple organizations and switch between them using the dropdown in the top-left corner of the application. Logging into Flows means accessing your personal account, which can be associated with multiple organizations.

[Environments](https://flows.sh/docs/environments) are isolated instances within your organization where you can publish and test workflows independently. Each environment has a unique environment key used to configure the Flows SDK. Common environments include development, staging, and production.

A workflow is a series of steps executed in a specific sequence, defined by the connections between [blocks](https://flows.sh/docs/blocks) and their conditions. In the workflow editor, you can add blocks, connect them, and configure their properties.

Workflows are version-controlled and can be published to individual environments.

[Blocks](https://flows.sh/docs/blocks) are the individual steps of a workflow. They can represent UI elements, logical steps, or actions. Each block has customizable properties that define its behavior and can be connected to other blocks to form a workflow.

[Block properties](https://flows.sh/docs/blocks/block-properties/overview) are the configurable fields available to editors when a block is added to a workflow. They map directly to the props defined in your components. For instance, a "banner block" might include properties like `title`, `description`, `button label`, `button link`, and `hide close button`.

[Components](https://flows.sh/docs/components/overview) are reusable UI elements that can be integrated into workflows within Flows to display information or interact with users. They contain properties and instructions, giving editors the power to create custom workflows. Each component must correspond to a matching component in your application.

Exit nodes are connectors that allow workflows to leave a block. They include logic to determine which path should be followed when exiting. For example, clicking a button might trigger an exit node that leads to another block.

Paths connect blocks in a workflow, starting from an exit node of one block and ending at an entry node of another. They define the sequence of the workflow.

A user is any person your application identifies to the Flows SDK using a `userId`. Flows uses this identifier to track user progress through workflows and store their state between sessions.

[User properties](https://flows.sh/docs/users/properties) are key-value pairs that describe a user, such as their plan, role, or account creation date. You can reference user properties in workflow conditions to control which users enter a given workflow.

An MTU (Monthly Tracked User) is a unique user who has experienced a Flows workflow within the current billing cycle. A user is counted as an MTU when the Flows SDK renders a component in their browser or when they enter a [Delay block](https://flows.sh/docs/blocks/logic-blocks/delay). MTUs are the primary billing metric, see [Billing](https://flows.sh/docs/billing) for details.

[Tours](https://flows.sh/docs/tours) are guided, step-by-step instructions designed to help users complete a specific task or understand a feature within your application. They are typically used for onboarding new users or highlighting new functionalities. Tours need to be part of a workflow.

[Slots](https://flows.sh/docs/blocks/block-properties/slot) are places in your application where Flows can render components. They need to be defined manually in your codebase and then they can be referenced in the workflow editor to render Slottable components.

Last updated on

# Workflows

Source: https://flows.sh/docs/workflows/overview

# Overview

Workflows are a series of steps executed in a specific sequence, defined by the connections between blocks and their conditions.


Workflows allow you to create complex multi-step experiences that can span multiple sessions or even the entire user lifecycle. They are more versatile than tours and can operate independently of user interaction. Workflows can include logic, actions, and conditions that tours do not.

To create a workflow click the **New workflow** button at the **Workflows** page. You can then add blocks, connect them, and configure their properties.

Apart from the blocks and their properties, workflows have additional settings.

The **Frequency** setting allows you to define how often the workflow should be triggered. The workflow frequency can be configured in two places:

- When [publishing](https://flows.sh/docs/workflows/publishing)a workflow version, you can choose the frequency that will be applied to the environments where the version is published.
- In the [workflow settings](https://flows.sh/docs/workflows/publishing#managing-active-versions), you can change the frequency setting for each environment.

**Frequency options:**

- **Once**: The workflow is triggered only once for each user.
- **Every time**: The workflow is triggered every time the conditions are met and the user is not already in the workflow.

A workflow can have different versions active in different environments. You can publish a workflow to individual environments, allowing you to test changes before making them available to all users. When you are [publishing](https://flows.sh/docs/workflows/publishing) a workflow version, you can select the environments where the version should be active. To see which versions are active in specific environments, click the **environments** button in the workflow detail.

You can track how your workflows perform in the Analytics tab. Here you’ll find metrics such as how many users entered, completed, or stopped a workflow, along with both total and unique counts for each.

By default, analytics are shown across all versions and environments for the last 30 days. You can adjust this view using the filters at the top to change the date range, focus on a specific version, or filter by environment.

To view analytics for individual blocks, first select a specific version. Once selected, each block in the workflow editor will display its own metrics. Clicking on a block opens a more detailed view of its analytics.


Workflows are version-controlled. When you make changes to a workflow, they are saved in a working `draft` version. You can then publish this version to individual environments. This allows you to test changes before making them available to all users. To see a list of versions, click the three dots in the top right corner of the workflow detail and select **Version history**. From the page that opens, you can:

- See all past versions of the current workflow
- Click on any past version to see how the workflow looked at that time

You can view published versions and their block configurations in a read-only mode. To edit a workflow switch back to the `draft` version and make changes.

Each version has its own `user migration` settings. The [user migration settings](https://flows.sh/docs/workflows/publishing#how-to-migrate-active-users) are applied to the users of the environment every time the specific version is activated in the environment.

Looking to revert to a previous version? [Contact us](https://flows.sh/contact) and we'll be happy to help!

Last updated on

# Blocks

Source: https://flows.sh/docs/blocks

# Blocks

Understand the blocks that power your workflows.


Blocks define the behavior of a workflow. They can represent UI elements, logical steps, or actions. Each block has customizable properties that define its behavior and can be connected to other blocks to form a workflow.

The connections between blocks (paths) determine how users navigate through the process.

In Flows there are different types of blocks based on their functionality.


### Start

The start of every workflow.


### Tour

Used to guide users through a series of steps.


### Built-in components

Pixel-perfect components for building product adoption.


### Custom components

Create and use your own custom components.


### Logic

Define branching logic, conditions, and other rules.


### Action

Perform actions in response to workflow events.


### End

Exits the workflow.

# Basics V2 components

Source: https://flows.sh/docs/blocks/basics-v2/overview

# Overview

A set of essential UI components to kickstart your product adoption journey.


**Basics V2** provides a set of ready-to-use and pixel-perfect components (**Modal**, **Tooltip**, and **Hint**) for building onboarding and education flows in your product. Each component integrates seamlessly with Flows, handling rendering, state, and lifecycle so you can focus on your app’s logic and UI.


### Tooltip

Guide users with helpful tooltips.


### Modal

Display a modal to guide users through a process.


### Hint

Provide subtle hints to users.


### Card

Show information or drive action with inline cards.


### Floating Checklist

Drive setup and activation with a list of instructions and tasks.


### Survey Popover

Collect feedback and insights inside your product.

Looking for more components? [Contact us](https://flows.sh/contact) and let us know what you'd like to see in future releases!

You can install and integrate the Basics V2 library using either [React](https://flows.sh#react) or [JavaScript](https://flows.sh#javascript), depending on your application stack.

In the Flows dashboard, go to **Components** and click the **Libraries** button. In the dialog that appears, find the Basics V2 library and click **Enable library**.

Once enabled, you’ll see the Basics V2 components available when adding new blocks to a workflow.

The Basics V2 components come with default styles, but you can easily customize them to match your product’s design. See the [styling guide](https://flows.sh/docs/blocks/basics-v2/styling) for details on how to override styles and use your own CSS.

For Flows to be able to render the components from the Basics V2 library, you need to setup the slot components and render function for the floating blocks. Rendering of slot blocks will be handled by the [flows-slot](https://flows.sh/docs/sdk/javascript/reference#flows-slot) element.

Add `<flows-floating-blocks>` custom element at the end of the `<body>` tag.

In the Flows dashboard, go to **Components** and click the **Libraries** button. In the dialog that appears, find the Basics V2 library and click **Enable library**.

Once enabled, you’ll see the Basics V2 components available when adding new blocks to a workflow.

The Basics V2 components come with default styles, but you can easily customize them to match your product’s design. See the [styling guide](https://flows.sh/docs/blocks/basics-v2/styling) for details on how to override styles and use your own CSS.

If you're currently using the **Basics V1** library, upgrading to **Basics V2** is simple. The new version introduces improved design, better functionality, and a familiar API. However, there are a few **breaking changes** requiring you to manually update in your workflows.

Both libraries can run **side-by-side**, allowing you to gradually migrate without disrupting your existing setup.

Make sure you're using the latest version of the main `@flows/react` SDK to ensure compatibility with Basics V2.

To use both versions simultaneously, alias the V1 package in your `package.json`:

This setup prevents conflicts and lets you import both versions in parallel.

You can now import both versions and register them with the `FlowsProvider`.

Alias your V1 imports to avoid naming conflicts. Because V1 and V2 components have distinct names, you can safely use both in parallel until migration is complete.

In the Flows dashboard, go to **Components** and click the **Libraries** button. In the dialog that appears:

- Disable the Basics V1 library.
- Enable the Basics V2 library.

This makes the new V2 components available when adding new blocks, without affecting existing workflows. The V1 components just won't be available when adding new blocks.

Unfortunately, due to the breaking changes between the two versions, there is no way for us to automatically migrate your existing workflows. You’ll need to manually replace V1 components with their V2 equivalents:

- Open a workflow using V1 components.
- Remove the V1 blocks and add the corresponding V2 blocks.
- Republish the workflow.

For short-lived or temporary workflows, you might simply leave them as-is and use V2 for all new workflows going forward.

The JavaScript package in Basics V2 is a complete rewrite, featuring a new rendering approach. Because of that, we recommend completely replacing the V1 package with the V2 package instead of trying to run both side-by-side. To migrate:

- Update the main `@flows/js`SDK to the latest version to ensure compatibility with Basics V2.
- Follow the [JavaScript installation guide](https://flows.sh#javascript)above to set up the V2 package.
- Update your workflows to use the V2 components.
- Once verified, release the update to production.

# Tours

Source: https://flows.sh/docs/tours

# Tours

Guide users through your application with step-by-step, interactive experiences.


Tours are guided, step-by-step instructions designed to help users complete a specific task or understand a feature within your application. They are often used for onboarding [users](https://flows.sh/docs/users/overview) or introducing new features. Tours must be integrated into a [workflow](https://flows.sh/docs/workflows/overview).

Tours can be created only as a part of a workflow. To create a tour, follow these steps:

- Add a tour block to an existing workflow using the **Add block**menu.
- Configure each step to define the sequence and content of the tour.
- Save and publish your workflow to make the tour available to users.

Although both tours and workflows use blocks, their purposes differ:

- **Tours**: Linear, step-by-step instructions designed to help users complete a specific task or understand a feature.
- **Workflows**: Versatile processes supporting complex sequences with logic, actions, and conditions.

When choosing between a tour and a workflow, consider:

- If the sequence is short and needs to be completed in one session, use a **tour**.
- For longer or multi-session sequences, use a **workflow**.

Tours are designed to provide a better user experience for step-by-step instructions. Their main benefits include:

- **Low latency**: When a tour is started, the whole sequence is loaded into the user's browser, making switching between steps instant.
- **Forwards and backwards navigation**: Users can navigate to the previous steps, making it easier to review instructions.
- **State persistence**: Tours remember the user's progress, even if they leave and return later.

Tours consist of tour-specific blocks from your block library. Each step behaves like a standard block but includes built-in connections to the previous and next steps through `previous` and `continue` exit nodes. A `cancel` exit node allows users to exit the tour at any step. See the [tour block](https://flows.sh/docs/blocks/tour-block) documentation for more details.

Learn how the tour block works and how to configure it in the [tour block](https://flows.sh/docs/blocks/tour-block) documentation.

Last updated on

---

# Surveys

Source: https://flows.sh/docs/surveys/overview

# Overview

Collect structured feedback from users directly within your application.


Surveys let you collect structured feedback from users at any point in a [workflow](https://flows.sh/docs/workflows/overview). You can ask users to rate their experience, choose from options, or leave freeform comments - all without leaving your application.

Surveys can only be created as part of a workflow. To create a survey:

- Add a survey block to an existing workflow using the **Add block**menu.
- Add questions and configure each one.
- Select a component under **Presentation**to define how the survey is displayed to users.
- Configure any additional settings such as targeting, triggers, or component properties.
- Save and publish your workflow to make the survey available to users.

For a detailed walkthrough, see the [Create a Survey guide](https://flows.sh/docs/guides/create-survey).

The trigger property defines when the survey should appear. By default, the survey starts automatically when the user reaches the survey block in a workflow. However, you can configure custom triggers to show the survey based on specific conditions.

Trigger conditions are defined as an array, and all conditions must be met for the survey to start. The following trigger types are supported:

- **User navigates to a page**- the survey starts when the user navigates to a specified URL.
- **User clicks on an element**- the survey starts when the user clicks a specific element (use CSS selector).
- **Element is on the page**- the survey starts when a specific element is present in the DOM (use CSS selector).
- **Element is not on the page**- the survey starts when a specific element is not present in the DOM (use CSS selector).


The **Presentation** setting controls which component renders the survey UI to your users. You must select a component before the survey can be displayed.

You can choose from custom components you have built in your [component library](https://flows.sh/docs/components/overview), or from built-in library components. The selected component is shared across all languages - it cannot be configured per language.

Changing the component after initial setup will overwrite any existing component properties and require you to reconfigure them from scratch.


Each survey is made up of one or more questions. You can mix and match question types within a single survey. Use the **Add question** menu inside the survey block to add a new question.

Freeform questions accept open-ended text input from the user.

**Options:**

- **Placeholder**- hint text displayed inside the text field before the user starts typing.


Rating questions ask users to select a value on a numerical scale.

**Options:**

- **Display**- the visual style of the rating input:- **Numbers**- a row of numbered buttons.
- **Stars**- star icons.
- **Emojis**- emoji icons.
 
- **Scale**- the range of values. Available options depend on the display type:- Numbers: 1-3, 1-5, 1-7, 1-10, 0-10 (NPS)
- Stars and Emojis: 1-3, 1-5
 
- **Lower label**- label shown at the low end of the scale (e.g. "Poor").
- **Upper label**- label shown at the high end of the scale (e.g. "Excellent").


Single choice questions present a list of options and allow the user to select one.

**Options:**

- **Options**- the list of choices. You can add, edit, remove, and reorder options.
- **Shuffle options**- randomize the order in which options are shown to users.
- **Other option**- adds a free-text "Other" field below the options list. You can customize the label for this field.


Multiple choice questions work the same as single choice, but allow the user to select more than one option.

**Options:**

- **Options**- the list of choices. You can add, edit, remove, and reorder options.
- **Shuffle options**- randomize the order in which options are shown to users.
- **Other option**- adds a free-text "Other" field below the options list. You can customize the label for this field.


Link questions display a call-to-action button. Use them to send users to a relevant resource or to confirm they have acknowledged something.

**Options:**

- **Button label**- the text shown on the button.
- **URL**- the destination URL. If left empty, the button acts as an acknowledgement with no navigation.
- **Open in new tab**- whether to open the URL in a new browser tab.


The end screen is the final step of a survey. It confirms to the user that their response has been submitted. There can only be one end screen per survey and it is always displayed last.

**Options:**

- **Button label**- the text shown on the button (e.g. "Done").
- **URL**- an optional link to open when the button is clicked.


All question types share the following properties:

- **Title**- the question text shown to the user. Required.
- **Description**- optional supporting text shown below the title.
- **Optional**- when enabled, users can skip the question without providing an answer.

To reorder questions, hover over a question and drag it by the handle that appears on the left side. The end screen question is always pinned to the last position.

Survey results are available in the analytics tab of the survey block. See the [analytics](https://flows.sh/docs/surveys/analytics) page for details.

- Follow the [Create a Survey guide](https://flows.sh/docs/guides/create-survey)for a step-by-step walkthrough of building and publishing your first survey using the Survey Popover component.
- Explore the [Survey Popover example](https://flows.sh/examples/survey-popover)to see a fully built survey in action and access the source code.

Last updated on

# Components

Source: https://flows.sh/docs/components/overview

# Overview

Display information and interact with users using reusable UI components in Flows.


Components are reusable UI elements that can be integrated into [workflows](https://flows.sh/docs/workflows/overview) within Flows to display information or interact with users. They contain properties and instructions, giving editors the power to create custom workflows. Each component must correspond to a matching component in your application.

# Users

Source: https://flows.sh/docs/users/overview

# Overview

Inspect user activity and manage their workflow states.


Users are individuals who you identify inside Flows. Each user has a unique identifier and can experience [workflows](https://flows.sh/docs/workflows/overview) inside your app. Users are scoped on environment level, meaning that a user with the same ID will have individual user profile and workflow states in each environment.

The **User detail** page allows you to:

Users are automatically added to Flows when they are initialized in your application. When you identify a user, Flows creates a user profile based on the provided user ID. You can't add users manually.

Currently users can't be removed from Flows. If you need to remove a user, contact us at [support@flows.sh](mailto:support@flows.sh).

# Environments

Source: https://flows.sh/docs/environments

# Environments

Separate Flows deployments for different stages of your development lifecycle.


Environments allow you to manage [workflows](https://flows.sh/docs/workflows/overview) across the entire development lifecycle, from local development to production. Each environment operates independently with its own:

- Active workflow versions and statuses
- Workflow analytics
- Users

You can create an unlimited number of environments.

To create a new environment:

- Navigate to **Settings > Environment**.
- Enter a **unique key**for the environment. This key is used to identify the environment in the SDK.

To modify an existing environment:

- Navigate to **Settings > Environment**.
- Update the **environment key**as needed.

**Important:** If you update the environment key, ensure the key is updated in your SDK setup to
prevent service disruptions.

Each environment is associated with a unique key that links your application to the correct workflows. Include this key in your SDK setup:

# Localization

Source: https://flows.sh/docs/localization

# Localization

Localize your workflows to support multiple languages and regions.


Localize your workflows and tours to support multiple languages and regions. Internationalization (i18n) allows you to adapt your content to different languages, cultures, and regions, ensuring a better user experience for diverse audiences.

Localization features are hidden until you add a second language group to your organization. To
enable localization, go to **Organization settings** > **Localization** and create a new language
group.

When editing blocks in a workflow you can switch between different languages using the language switcher below the block name in the right sidebar. To switch languages:

- Select a block in the workflow editor.
- Use the language switcher below the block name in the right sidebar.
- Choose the desired language from the dropdown menu (green dot indicates a translation exists, grey dot means a translation is missing).
- Click `Create translation`if no translation exists for the selected language.
- Edit content and properties in the selected language.


Each block in a workflow can have translations for multiple languages. To add a translation:

- Select a block in the workflow editor.
- Switch to the language you want to add using the language switcher.
- Click on the `Create translation`button that appears after switching languages.

This will create a new translation for the block in the selected language. You can then edit the content and properties of the block in that language.


To remove a translation:

- Select a block in the workflow editor.
- Switch to the language you want to remove.
- Click on the trash icon next to the language name and confirm the removal.

This will remove the translation for that block in the selected language, and the block will fall back to the default language of your organization.


Localization is available only for **Component blocks** and **Tour blocks**. Supported block properties are `string`, `number`, `boolean`, and `select`. Unsupported blocks and properties will be the same for all language groups. You can identify unsupported blocks and properties by the globe icon next to them in the block editor.


To add a new language group:

- Go to **Organization settings > Localization**.
- Click on **New language group**.
- Name the group and add relevant languages to it.

The new language group will become available in the workflow editor, allowing you to create translations for blocks in that group. Until you add translations for the new group, it will fall back to the default language group.


When a user enters a block, Flows will first check if the block has a translation for the users language group. If a translation exists, it will be used. If there is no matching translation, Flows will fall back to the default language group.

For languages that are read from right to left (RTL), such as Arabic or Hebrew, Flows doesn't automatically apply RTL styles. You need to handle RTL languages in your custom components by applying the appropriate style changes. For example, you can use a boolean property in your custom component to indicate whether the language is RTL or not, and then apply the necessary styles based on that property.

If needed, you can create distinct workflows for each language. This gives you full control over content and structure in each version. However, it requires more upkeep if you want to keep workflows synchronized across languages.

Last updated on

# Personalization

# Personalization

Personalize your workflows using user properties.


Personalization allows you to customize workflows based on user properties such as name, plan, or preferences. By leveraging these properties, you can create more engaging and relevant experiences for your users. For example, you can use a customer name in a message or link to a dynamic URL that includes user's ID.

Personalization uses any user properties that are available to the Flows SDK. To get started, ensure that your application is passing the necessary user properties to the SDK. [Learn more about user properties](https://flows.sh/docs/users/properties).

To insert user properties into your workflow, use the personalization syntax `{{ property_name }}`. Replace `property_name` with the actual name of the user property you want to use. For example, to include the user's first name in a welcome message, you would write:

This will dynamically replace `{{ first_name }}` with the actual first name of the user when the block is rendered.

Sometimes, a user property might not be available for the current user. In such cases, you can provide a fallback value to ensure that your message still makes sense. To add a fallback value, use the pipe symbol `|` followed by the fallback text. For example:

If the `first_name` property is not available, the message will default to `Hi, there`.

# Launchpad

Source: https://flows.sh/docs/launchpad

# Launchpad

Air traffic control for your workflows.


Launchpad is like an air traffic control for your workflows. Create groups to manage workflow priorities, set concurrency limits, and get better control over all your workflows.

To create a Launchpad group, visit the **Launchpad** page in the Flows dashboard and click **New group**. Enter a name for the group and confirm. Once created, you can add workflows, ordered them by priority, and set concurrency limits. When the group is ready, click **Save group**.


Users enter workflows in a Launchpad group based on priority. Workflows higher in the list are started first. You can reorder workflows by dragging and dropping them in the **Workflows** section of the Launchpad group detail page. This is useful for prioritizing important workflows (e.g., onboarding > upsells > surveys).

Note that workflow priority doesn't guarantee that workflows will always start in that order. Launchpad groups are used to determine which workflows to start when criteria are met, but other factors like already running workflows and concurrency limits also play a role.


Concurrency limits how many workflows from the group can run at the same time. The concurrency can either be unlimited or limited to a specific number. If the limit is reached, the group will wait until a running workflow finishes before starting a new one. This is useful for avoiding overwhelming users with too many workflows at once.


Launchpad groups can be paused to prevent workflows from starting while allowing already running workflows to finish. To pause a group switch its state in the top right corner from enabled to paused and save the group.

Note: Pausing a group does not affect already running workflows. They will continue to run until they finish. To stop already running workflows, you have to disable the workflow itself.


When multiple Launchpad groups are enabled, they are evaluated in order from top to bottom. You can reorder groups by dragging and dropping them in the **Launchpad** page. This is useful when you have one workflow in multiple groups and want to control which group should have the potential to start the workflow first.


Workflows that are not part of any Launchpad group are started immediately when their Start block criteria are met. They are not subject to Launchpad group priorities or concurrency limits. This is useful for workflows that need to run instantly, such as critical alerts or notifications, or when you don't have many workflows and don't need the extra control provided by Launchpad groups.

Last updated on

# Billing

Source: https://flows.sh/docs/billing

# Billing

We offer a free plan and pay-as-you-go plan to suit your needs.


Flows offers a **Forever Free** plan with generous usage limits, ideal for startups and small teams. When you're ready to scale, our **Pay-As-You-Go** plan ensures flexibility with costs based on actual usage. For the most up-to-date information, visit our [pricing page](https://flows.sh/pricing).

Billing is calculated based on Monthly Tracked Users (MTUs) across all [environments](https://flows.sh/docs/environments) in your organization. You are billed monthly, and subscriptions can be canceled anytime.

**Pay-As-You-Go:** Costs are based on the total MTUs during the billing period. A monthly cycle begins on your subscription date and renews on the same day each month. For example, if you subscribe on the 15th, your next cycle will start on the 15th of the following month. The MTU (Monthly Tracked User) count resets 24 hours before the next billing cycle begins. This window ensures all usage data is properly processed and finalized for accurate invoicing.

**Free Plan:** Usage limits reset at the start of every month. If you reach the limit, you cannot identify new [users](https://flows.sh/docs/users/overview) until the next cycle, but existing users continue to access workflows without interruption.

MTUs are the number of unique users that have experienced a Flows workflow in the current billing cycle. Individual users are counted based on the `userId` you provide in the Flows SDK.

**User is counted if:**

- The Flows SDK has rendered a component in their browser
- The user has entered a [Delay block](https://flows.sh/docs/blocks/logic-blocks/delay)in a workflow

**User is not counted if:**

- They have entered a workflow, but no components have been rendered.
- They are active in a workflow but have not visited your product in the current billing cycle.
- They are not active in any workflow.
- They have not visited your product in the current billing cycle.

If a user is counted as MTU, they can experience any number of workflows in the current billing cycle.

To manage your subscription, navigate to **Settings > Billing**, where you can:

- Upgrade or downgrade your plan
- Update payment or billing contact information
- Review billing history, invoices, and payments

Navigate to **Settings > Billing** and select **Upgrade**. Your new plan takes effect immediately, starting a new billing cycle from the day you upgrade.

To cancel a subscription, navigate to **Settings > Billing**. Your subscription will be canceled immediately, and your usage limit will revert to the Free tier. The last invoice will be generated at the end of the billing cycle.

The **Pay-As-You-Go** plan includes the option to set usage limits to avoid surprises. Configure these limits in the **Usage Limit** section of **Settings > Billing**.

- Notifications are sent when you reach 80% and 100% of your limit.
- Once the limit is reached, new users will not be identified until the next billing cycle or the limit is increased. Users already counted in MTUs can continue to experience workflows without interruption.

To add a VAT number during checkout, choose the **Add tax ID number** option.

To add a VAT number for an existing subscription, navigate to **Settings > Billing** and click the **Manage subscription** button. You will be redirected to your Customer portal in Lemon Squeezy where you can add your VAT number.

To update your payment information or billing contact, navigate to **Settings > Billing** and click the **Manage subscription** button. You will be redirected to your Customer portal in Lemon Squeezy where you can update your payment information or billing contact.

Are you a startup, non-profit, or educational institution? Contact us at [hello@flows.sh](mailto:hello@flows.sh) for details about special pricing.

Last updated on

# React SDK reference

Source: https://flows.sh/docs/sdk/react/reference

# Reference

Discover methods and types available in the @flows/react and @flows/react-components packages.

Flows React SDK is a library that allows you to integrate Flows into React applications.

Install the package [from npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@flows/react):

The `<FlowsProvider />` component is the main component of the Flows SDK. It initializes the SDK and keeps track of the user's state.

The `<FlowsProvider />` accepts the following props:

| Name | Type | Required | Notes | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `organizationId` | `string` | Yes | Your organization ID. Find this in Settings > General. | 
| `environment` | `string` | Yes | The environment key. Find this in Settings > Environments. | 
| `userId` | `string` | No | Unique ID used to identify the user. If set to `null`, the SDK will be disabled and`children`will render while waiting for the`userId`. This is useful when loading the ID asynchronously. | 
| `components` | `object` | Yes | Custom components to use in your workflows. | 
| `tourComponents` | `object` | Yes | Custom tour components to use in tour blocks. | 
| `surveyComponents` | `object` | Yes | Custom survey components to use in survey blocks. | 
| `userProperties` | `object` | No | Object with custom [user properties](https://flows.sh/docs/users/properties). Values can be`string`,`number`,`boolean`, or`date`. | 
| `language` | `LanguageOption` | No | The user's language used for [localization](https://flows.sh/docs/localization). When empty the user will receive the default language group. | 
| `apiUrl` | `string` | No | Custom API URL useful when using proxy to send Flows requests through your own domain. | 
| `debug` | `boolean` | No | Enable [debug mode](https://flows.sh/docs/sdk/debug)to inspect the SDK's behavior. | 
| `onDebugShortcut` | `function` | No | Custom keyboard shortcut handler for opening the debug panel. By default, the debug panel opens with `Cmd + Option + Shift + F`on Mac or`Ctrl + Alt + Shift + F`on Windows/Linux. If you set this prop, the default shortcut will not work. | 
| `LinkComponent` | `LinkComponentType` | No | Custom Link component used for client-side navigation when using components from `@flows/react-components`. Otherwise each link click will result in a full page reload. | 

The `<FlowsSlot />` is a component used to create Slots in your app where you can insert components using Workflows. [Learn more about using Slots](https://flows.sh/docs/blocks/block-properties/slot) in the Flows editor.

| Name | Type | Required | Notes | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` | Yes | The Slot ID used to refer to the slot when creating workflows. | 
| `placeholder` | `ReactNode` | No | The component to render when no component is inserted in the slot. | 
| `limit` | `number` | No | Limit of how many blocks to render in the slot. Defaults to no limit. | 

The `<Block />` component renders a single [ ActiveBlock](https://flows.sh#activeblock) using the matching component registered in 

`<FlowsProvider />`. It looks up the right component from `components`, `tourComponents`, or `surveyComponents` based on the block type.Use `<Block />` when you need custom rendering logic beyond what `<FlowsSlot />` provides — for example, to wrap blocks in a custom container, apply animations, or control rendering order yourself.

The `useCurrentFloatingBlocks()` hook returns the active floating blocks for the user in the current environment.

Parameters: None

Returns:

An array of [ ActiveBlock](https://flows.sh#activeblock) objects representing the current floating blocks.

The `useCurrentSlotBlocks()` hook returns the active slottable blocks for the user in the current environment.

Parameters:

| Name | Type | Required | Notes | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `slotId` | `string` | Yes | The ID of the slot to query. You can find it in the Flows app in the slot detail. | 

Returns:

An array of [ ActiveBlock](https://flows.sh#activeblock) objects representing the current slottable blocks for the specified slot.

Starts a workflow for the current user in the current environment using a the block key of a manual start block. The workflow will start only if:

- Workflow is published in the current environment
- Workflow has a manual start block with a matching block key
- The current user can access the workflow based on the frequency setting
- The current user matches the start block's user property conditions

Parameters:

| Name | Type | Required | Notes | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `blockKey` | `string` | Yes | The block key of the manual start block you want to trigger. [Learn more](https://flows.sh/docs/blocks/start-blocks/manual-start) | 

Returns: `Promise<void>`

The `resetWorkflowProgress()` function resets the progress of a specific workflow for the current user in the current environment.

Parameters:

| Name | Type | Required | Notes | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `workflowId` | `string` | Yes | The ID of the workflow to reset. You can find it in the Flows app in the workflow detail. | 

The `resetAllWorkflowsProgress()` function resets the progress of all workflows for the current user in the current environment.

Parameters: None

Returns all available workflows for the current user. Before calling this method, the `<FlowsProvider>` component must be rendered. Only enabled workflows are returned.

Parameters: None

Returns: `Promise<``WorkflowsResponse``>`

Represents a block visible to the user.

| Name | Type | Notes | 
|---|---|---|

Represents the survey object provided to survey components.

| Name | Type | Required | Notes | 
|---|---|---|---|

| `nextQuestion` | `function` | Yes | Advances to the next question and returns the new index. Method for optional built-in question navigation. |

| `description` | `string` | No | Description of the question. May contain HTML. | 
| `optional` | `boolean` | Yes | Whether the user may skip the question. | 
| `options` | `{ id: string; label: string }[]` | Yes | Ordered list of available options. | 
| `otherOption` | `boolean` | Yes | Whether an additional "other" option should be rendered. | 
| `otherLabel` | `string` | No | Label for the "other" option. | 
| `getSelectedOptionIds` | `function` | Yes | Returns the ids of all currently selected options. | 
| `setSelectedOptionIds` | `function` | Yes | Sets the currently selected option ids. | 
| `getValue` | `function` | Yes | Returns the current text value for the "other" option. | 
| `setValue` | `function` | Yes | Sets the current text value for the "other" option. | 
| `getOtherSelected` | `function` | Yes | Returns whether the "other" option is currently selected. | 
| `setOtherSelected` | `function` | Yes | Sets whether the "other" option is selected. | 

Represents a rating survey question.

| Name | Type | Required | Notes | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` | Yes | Unique identifier for the question. | 
| `type` | `"rating"` | Yes | The question type. | 
| `title` | `string` | Yes | Title of the question. May contain HTML. | 
| `description` | `string` | No | Description of the question. May contain HTML. | 
| `optional` | `boolean` | Yes | Whether the user may skip the question. | 
| `displayType` | `"numbers" | "stars" | "emojis"` | Yes | Visual style of the rating buttons. | 
| `minValue` | `number` | Yes | Minimum selectable value on the rating scale. | 
| `maxValue` | `number` | Yes | Maximum selectable value on the rating scale. | 
| `lowerBoundLabel` | `string` | No | Label shown at the low end of the rating scale. | 
| `upperBoundLabel` | `string` | No | Label shown at the high end of the rating scale. | 
| `getValue` | `function` | Yes | Returns the selected rating value as a numeric string. | 
| `setValue` | `function` | Yes | Sets the selected rating value using a numeric string. | 

Represents a link survey question.

| Name | Type | Required | Notes | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` | Yes | Unique identifier for the question. | 
| `type` | `"link"` | Yes | The question type. | 
| `title` | `string` | Yes | Title of the question. May contain HTML. | 
| `description` | `string` | No | Description of the question. May contain HTML. | 
| `optional` | `boolean` | Yes | Whether the user may skip the question. | 
| `linkLabel` | `string` | Yes | Label for the clickable link shown to the user. | 
| `url` | `string` | Yes | URL the user is navigated to when they click the link. | 
| `openInNew` | `boolean` | Yes | Whether the link opens in a new browser tab. | 
| `setClicked` | `function` | Yes | Marks the link question as clicked so the interaction is recorded. | 

Represents the final survey screen.

| Name | Type | Required | Notes | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` | Yes | Unique identifier for the question. | 
| `type` | `"end-screen"` | Yes | The question type. | 
| `title` | `string` | Yes | Title of the screen. May contain HTML. | 
| `description` | `string` | No | Description of the screen. May contain HTML. | 
| `optional` | `boolean` | Yes | Whether the user may skip the screen. | 
| `linkLabel` | `string` | No | Label for the optional link shown on the end screen. | 
| `url` | `string` | No | URL the user is navigated to from the end screen link. | 
| `openInNew` | `boolean` | Yes | Whether the link opens in a new browser tab. | 

Represents the `__flows` object included in component props.

| Name | Type | Required | Notes | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `__flows.id` | `string` | Yes | Unique identifier of the block, useful for stable key during rendering. Keep in mind each workflow version will have a different id for each block. | 
| `__flows.key` | `string` | No | Unique key for the block. Set by you in a workflow. [Learn more](https://flows.sh/docs/blocks/block-properties/block-key) | 
| `__flows.workflowId` | `string` | Yes | The ID of the workflow. Set by Flows. | 

The response returned by [ fetchWorkflows()](https://flows.sh#fetchworkflows).

Represents a workflow and its state for the current user.

| Name | Type | Required | Notes | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` | Yes | The ID of the workflow. | 
| `workflow_status` | `WorkflowStatus` | Yes | The publish status of the workflow. | 
| `frequency` | `WorkflowFrequency` | Yes | How often the workflow can be entered. | 
| `user_state` | `WorkflowUserState` | Yes | The current user's state in the workflow. | 
| `entered_at` | `string` | No | ISO date string of when the user entered the workflow. | 
| `exited_at` | `string` | No | ISO date string of when the user exited the workflow. | 

The publish status of a workflow. Returned in the [ Workflow](https://flows.sh#workflow) object.

- `"enabled"`- The workflow is published and active.
- `"launchpad-enabled"`- The workflow is published, active, and inside an active launchpad group.

How often a workflow can be entered by a user. Returned in the [ Workflow](https://flows.sh#workflow) object.

- `"once"`- The workflow can only be entered once.
- `"every-time"`- The workflow can be entered every time.

The current user's state in a workflow. Returned in the [ Workflow](https://flows.sh#workflow) object.

- `"not-started"`- The user has not entered the workflow.
- `"in-progress"`- The user is currently in the workflow.
- `"completed"`- The user has completed the workflow.
- `"stopped"`- The user has been stopped in- **the**workflow (e.g., by a workflow migration).

Language type used for setting the user's language in the `<FlowsProvider />` to enable [localization](https://flows.sh/docs/localization).

Options:

- `disabled`(default) - The user will be served content in the default language group of your organization.
- `automatic`- Automatically detect the user's language and use the matching language group. The language is determined by the- `Navigator.language`property in the browser.
- Manual - A specific language string, e.g. `en-US`,`fr-FR`, etc. This will use the matching language group for the specified language. See[https://www.localeplanet.com/icu/](https://www.localeplanet.com/icu/)for a full list of supported languages.

The type for the `LinkComponent` prop in the `<FlowsProvider />`. See [ LinkComponentProps](https://flows.sh#linkcomponentprops) for more details.

`type LinkComponentType = React.FC<LinkComponentProps>`

Props passed to `LinkComponent` prop in the `<FlowsProvider />`. `LinkComponent` is used for client-side navigation when using components from `@flows/react-components`, preventing full page reloads.

| Name | Type | Required | Notes | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `href` | `string` | Yes | The destination URL. | 
| `children` | `ReactNode` | No | The link content. | 
| `className` | `string` | No | CSS class names. | 
| `onClick` | `function` | No | Click event handler. | 

Example implementation:

To simplify implementation, you can use the `@flows/react-components` package, which provides pre-built UI components.

Install the package [from npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@flows/react-components):

Then, import and use the components in your app:

# JavaScript SDK reference

Source: https://flows.sh/docs/sdk/javascript/reference

# Reference

Discover methods and types available in the @flows/js and @flows/js-components packages.

Flows JS SDK is a lightweight library that allows you to integrate Flows into any application that runs JavaScript.

Install the package [from npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@flows/js):

Initializes the `@flows/js` SDK and identifies the user. This method must be called at least once in your application.

Parameters:

| Name | Type | Required | Notes | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `organizationId` | `string` | Yes | Your organization ID, available in Settings > General. | 
| `environment` | `string` | Yes | The environment key, available in Settings > Environments. | 
| `userId` | `string` | Yes | Unique ID for identifying the user. | 
| `userProperties` | `object` | No | Object with custom [user properties](https://flows.sh/docs/users/properties)as key-value pairs. Accepts`string`,`number`,`boolean`, or`date`. | 
| `language` | `LanguageOption` | No | The user's language used for [localization](https://flows.sh/docs/localization). When empty the user will receive the default language group. | 
| `apiUrl` | `string` | No | Custom API URL for proxying requests through your domain. | 
| `debug` | `boolean` | No | Enable [debug mode](https://flows.sh/docs/sdk/debug)to inspect the SDK's behavior. | 
| `onDebugShortcut` | `function` | No | Custom keyboard shortcut handler for opening the debug panel. By default, the debug panel opens with `Cmd + Option + Shift + F`on Mac or`Ctrl + Alt + Shift + F`on Windows/Linux. If you set this prop, the default shortcut will not work. | 
| `onNavigate` | `OnNavigate` | No | Handler for intercepting internal link clicks inside Flows components. Use this to route navigation through your client-side router instead of triggering a full page reload. | 

Registers a listener for updates to floating workflow and tour blocks. Slottable blocks are not included.

Parameters:

Returns:

A function to unsubscribe the listener and avoid memory leaks.

Registers a listener for updates to blocks in a specific slot.

Parameters:

| Name | Type | Required | Notes | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `slotId` | `string` | Yes | Slot ID of the slot to monitor. | 
| `listener` | `function` | Yes | Callback function that receives updated array of .`ActiveBlock` | 

Returns:

A function to unsubscribe the listener and avoid memory leaks.

Retrieves all currently active floating workflow and tour blocks. Slot blocks are not included.

Parameters: None

Returns:

An array of [ ActiveBlock](https://flows.sh#activeblock) objects.

Retrieves all currently active blocks for a specific slot.

Parameters:

| Name | Type | Required | Notes | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `slotId` | `string` | Yes | Slot ID to query. | 

Returns:

An array of [ ActiveBlock](https://flows.sh#activeblock) objects.

Starts a workflow for the current user in the current environment using a the block key of a manual start block. The workflow will start only if:

- Workflow is published in the current environment
- Workflow has a manual start block with a matching block key
- The current user can access the workflow based on the frequency setting
- The current user matches the start block's user property conditions

Parameters:

| Name | Type | Required | Notes | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `blockKey` | `string` | Yes | The block key of the manual start block you want to trigger. [Learn more](https://flows.sh/docs/blocks/start-blocks/manual-start) | 

Returns: `Promise<void>`

The `resetWorkflowProgress()` function resets the progress of a specific workflow for the current user in the current environment.

Parameters:

| Name | Type | Required | Notes | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `workflowId` | `string` | Yes | The ID of the workflow to reset. You can find it in the Flows app in the workflow detail. | 

The `resetAllWorkflowsProgress()` function resets the progress of all workflows for the current user in the current environment.

Parameters: None

Returns all available workflows for the current user. Before calling this method, the `init()` method must be called first. Only enabled workflows are returned.

Parameters: None

Returns: `Promise<``WorkflowsResponse``>`

Represents a block visible to the user.

| Name | Type | Notes | 
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` | Internal identifier for the block. Changes with every workflow version, for persistent identifier use `props.__flows.key`. | 
| `type` | `"component" | "tour-component" | "survey"` | The block type. | 
| `component` | `string` | The UI component that should be used to render the block. | 
| `props` | |`ComponentProps`|`TourComponentProps``SurveyComponentProps` | Props passed to the component, including data and exit node callbacks. | 

Represents the props passed to a component. In addition to your custom props, it includes the `__flows` object with Flows properties.

Represents the [state memory](https://flows.sh/docs/blocks/block-properties/state-memory) property of a block.

| Name | Type | Required | Notes | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `boolean` | Yes | The value of the state memory. | 
| `setValue` | `function` | Yes | Callback to set the value of the state memory. | 
| `triggers` | `array` | Yes | Object with triggers to update the state memory. See table below. | 

`triggers` type:

| Name | Type | Required | Notes | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | `string` | Yes | The trigger type. Can be `manual`or`transition`. | 
| `blockId` | `string` | Yes | The block ID of the block that triggers the state memory. | 
| `blockKey` | `string` | No | The block key of the block that triggers the state memory. | 

Represents the props passed to a tour component. In addition to your custom props, it includes tour component exit nodes and the `__flows` object with Flows properties.

| Name | Type | Required | Notes | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `continue` | `function` | Yes | Callback to go to the next step. | 
| `previous` | `function` | No | Callback to go back to the previous step. | 
| `cancel` | `function` | Yes | Callback to cancel the tour. | 
| `__flows` | `FlowsProperties` | Yes | Object containing Flows properties for the block. | 

Represents the props passed to a survey component. In addition to your custom props, it includes the `survey` object, survey exit node callbacks, and the `__flows` object with Flows properties.

| Name | Type | Required | Notes | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | `Survey` | Yes | Survey data and helper methods for reading answers, navigating questions, and submitting responses. | 
| Custom block properties | Depends on the property type | Yes | The properties of the selected block in the workflow. The properties are defined on in the block. | 
| `complete` | `function` | Yes | Callback to exit the survey block with the `complete`exit node. | 
| `cancel` | `function` | Yes | Callback to exit the survey block with the `cancel`exit node. | 
| `__flows` | `FlowsProperties` | Yes | Object containing Flows properties for the block. | 

Represents the survey object provided to survey components.

| Name | Type | Required | Notes | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `questions` | `SurveyQuestion[]` | Yes | Ordered list of all survey questions. | 
| `getCurrentQuestionIndex` | `function` | Yes | Returns the zero-based index of the currently displayed question. Method for optional built-in question navigation. | 
| `nextQuestion` | `function` | Yes | Advances to the next question and returns the new index. Method for optional built-in question navigation. | 
| `previousQuestion` | `function` | Yes | Moves to the previous question and returns the new index. Method for optional built-in question navigation. | 
| `submit` | `function` | Yes | Submits the survey response. Use `complete()`separately to close the survey block. |

Handler type for intercepting internal link clicks inside Flows components. Passed as the `onNavigate` option to [init()](https://flows.sh#init).

| Name | Type | Notes | 
|---|---|---|
| `href` | `string` | The destination URL. Can be an absolute path (e.g. `/about`) or a relative URL (e.g.`?q=1`). Only called for internal links not opening in a new tab. | 
| `event` | `PointerEvent` | The pointer event that triggered the navigation. Call `event.preventDefault()`to prevent a full page reload. | 

Language type used for setting the user's language in the `init()` function to enable [localization](https://flows.sh/docs/localization).

Options:

- `disabled`(default) - The user will be served content in the default language group of your organization.
- `automatic`- Automatically detect the user's language and use the matching language group. The language is determined by the- `Navigator.language`property in the browser.
- Manual - A specific language string, e.g. `en-US`,`fr-FR`, etc. This will use the matching language group for the specified language. See[https://www.localeplanet.com/icu/](https://www.localeplanet.com/icu/)for a full list of supported languages.

To simplify implementation, you can use the `@flows/js-components` package, which provides pre-built UI components and utilities for block rendering.

Install the package [from npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@flows/js-components):

Defines custom elements for `flows-floating-blocks`, `flows-slot` and all the passed UI components.

Parameters:

| Name | Type | Required | Notes | 
|---|---|---|---|
| `components` | `object` | Yes | Components to use in your workflows. | 
| `tourComponents` | `object` | Yes | Components to use in tour blocks. | 
| `surveyComponents` | `object` | Yes | Components to use in survey blocks. | 

A custom HTML element for rendering floating workflow and tour blocks. For this custom element to function correctly, you need to call `setupJsComponents()`.

A custom HTML element for rendering slot blocks. Use the `data-slot-id` attribute to specify the slot. For this custom element to function correctly, you need to call `setupJsComponents()`.

# Examples

Source: https://flows.sh/examples

# Examples

Learn what good product onboarding and education looks like and explore how Flows makes building it simple and easy.


## Tour

Guide users along their journey through your product


## Floating checklist

Interactive list of suggested setup actions the user can take. Floating in the corner of the screen.


## Tooltip

Guide users through your app by anchoring contextual tooltips to UI elements


## Feature announcement

Let users know about new features with a full page announcement.


## Feature hint

Dismissible hint used to highlight a new feature in your product.


## Onboarding hub

A home in your app for user onboarding and help resources.


## Getting started dashboard

Show users learning resources and onboarding tips when they first sign up.


## Modal

A dialog to focus user attention on relevant information


## Interactive feature announcement

Show how your new feature works instead of just telling users about it.


## In-App Changelog

Add an in-app changelog to your product to inform users about new features and updates.


## Microsurvey

Capture quick in-app feedback with a microsurvey widget.


## Announcement banner

Add a dismissible announcement banner at the top of your app for feature launches.


## Net Promoter Score (NPS) survey

Collect Net Promoter Score feedback in your React app with a non-intrusive survey popover.


## Survey Popover

Collect user feedback with a non-intrusive survey popover that floats in the corner of the screen.


## Product-Market Fit (PMF) survey

Measure product-market fit in your React app with a non-intrusive survey popover using the Sean Ellis method.


## Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) survey

Collect Customer Satisfaction Score feedback in your React app with a non-intrusive survey popover.


## Customer Effort Score (CES) survey

Collect Customer Effort Score feedback in your React app with a non-intrusive survey popover.


## Hint

Self-guided contextual hints that help with feature discovery and education.


## Embedded tips

Inline contextual tips to help users learn about product and UI concepts


## New feature card

Announce new features or updates with a card that shows up in your app’s sidebar.


## New feature badge

Highlight new features in your application with a badge.


## Enterprise upsell

Nudge users to upgrade with an in-page promotion card


## Card

A custom card component built to render content inside your product, not above it.


## Product Hunt launch announcement

Launching your product on Product Hunt? Broadcast the launch inside your app.


## Churn prevention flow

Reduce cancellations with a multi-step churn prevention flow.

# GitHub SDK examples

Source: https://github.com/RBND-studio/flows-sdk/tree/main/examples

This directory contains examples of flows that can be used as a starting point for your own Flows implementation.

- [React Next.js](https://github.com/RBND-studio/flows-sdk/blob/main/examples/react/next)- A simple example of how to use Flows with React and Next.js.
- [React Router](https://github.com/RBND-studio/flows-sdk/blob/main/examples/react/vite)- A simple example of how to use Flows with React Router and Vite.
- [TanStack Start](https://github.com/RBND-studio/flows-sdk/blob/main/examples/react/tanstack)- A simple example of how to use Flows with React and TanStack Start
- [Vue Nuxt](https://github.com/RBND-studio/flows-sdk/blob/main/examples/vue/nuxt)- A simple example of how to use Flows with Vue and Nuxt.
- [Angular](https://github.com/RBND-studio/flows-sdk/blob/main/examples/angular)- A simple example of how to use Flows with Angular.
- [SvelteKit](https://github.com/RBND-studio/flows-sdk/blob/main/examples/svelte)- A simple example of how to use Flows with SvelteKit.
- [Lit](https://github.com/RBND-studio/flows-sdk/blob/main/examples/lit)- A simple example of how to use Flows with Lit.
- [SolidJS](https://github.com/RBND-studio/flows-sdk/blob/main/examples/solid)- A simple example of how to use Flows with SolidJS.
- [Ember](https://github.com/RBND-studio/flows-sdk/blob/main/examples/ember)- A simple example of how to use Flows with Ember.
- [Astro](https://github.com/RBND-studio/flows-sdk/blob/main/examples/astro)- A simple example of how to use Flows with Astro.
- [Electron React](https://github.com/RBND-studio/flows-sdk/blob/main/examples/electron/electron-forge-react)- A simple example of how to use Flows with Electron and React - based on Electron Forge with Webpack and React.
- [JavaScript CDN](https://github.com/RBND-studio/flows-sdk/blob/main/examples/js/cdn)- A simple example of how to use Flows with JavaScript without NPM by loading global script from CDN.

We actively encourage our community to raise issues and provide feedback. If you find an issue, please let us know by raising an issue in the repository.

An issue can be raised by clicking the 'Issues' tab at the top of the repository, followed by the Green 'New issue' button.

When submitting an issue, please thoroughly and concisely describe the problem you are experiencing so that we may easily understand and resolve the issue in a timely manner.

# Pricing

Source: https://flows.sh/pricing

PRICING

# Pay only for what you use

Flows offer a pay-as-you-go pricing that starts at $0/month with a generous free forever tier.

Flows uses a tiered pricing model, where the price per MTU decreases as your usage increases. When you reach each new tier threshold, any additional MTUs are billed at the lower rate.

First 250 MTUs

Free every month

251 - 500

$0.1000 per MTU

501 - 1.5k

$0.0500 per MTU

1.5k - 5k

$0.0350 per MTU

5k - 15k

$0.0250 per MTU

15k - 50k

$0.0175 per MTU

50k +

$0.0125 per MTU

## FAQs

We count an MTU as a unique user that has experienced a Flows workflow in the current billing cycle. We don’t count users that have only entered a workflow but haven’t experienced it.

If user experiences a workflow multiple times in a month, they are only counted once. And if that user doesn’t experience a workflow in the next month, they are not counted in your usage for that month.

Experiencing a workflow means that at least one component block has been rendered to the user or they have entered a paid block type (e.g. Delay block). [Learn more](https://flows.sh/docs/billing#how-do-we-calculate-monthly-tracked-users-mtus)

Flows offers volume based pricing, the more MTUs you have the less you pay. Every month you will be billed based on the number of your MTUs. To get an estimate of your monthly cost, use our pricing calculator above.

Free tier resets on the first day of the month. Paid plans billing cycle starts on the day of the month that you subscribe. For example, if you subscribe on the 15th, your billing cycle will start on the 15th of every month.

Yes, we offer a free tier for the first 250 MTUs. No credit card required. When you exceed the free tier, you will need to upgrade to a pay as you go plan starting at $0.1 per MTU.

We will. We're happy to assist you with moving your existing onboarding to Flows. When transitioning to Flows from another tool, we offer free usage to cover the transition period and avoid double billing.
